title: 1919 Prairie's rear range turns its tall gable to the street
items: 1904: the Marshall Field Jr. house's rear range is now roofed with its ridge running back from the street. Its tall stone-coped, finialled gable faces Prairie Avenue and rises over the middle range, where all three Gatlin Institute plates draw it.

Seen from the avenue, the old gable facing the side yard sat 1-2 m too low and too far back. The new gable's peak now lands on the plates' within a few pixels, including the 1912 plate, which was not used to fit it.
Still to come: the two small pinnacled dormers on the flank and the stone block at the middle range's corner.
